fidelity.r1: FAITHFUL with minor deviations: (i) 7 unparseable 1ax corrections ('norm.status (…)') are applied to junk keys and listed as applied, contrary to 'REPORTED, never applied'; (ii) correction values are inserted verbatim incl. annotations ('null (NOT_EVIDENCED)' counts as a KNOWN actor); (iii) possible_pairs silently truncated to 12; (iv) a within-section pair counts as a one-cluster set in disjoint(). None changes an r1 verdict.
fidelity.r2: FAITHFUL to its declared changes. The exec composition really re-binds coding (same dict object, mutated in place), sect, lin (mutated in ns) and rows (ns globals). The mapping keys match MAPPING/REVIEW-1ayn, and UNMAPPABLE/missing becomes UNKNOWN. The R06/R07 merge is as specified. Undeclared side effects: the mapping overwrites 1ax reviewer corrections (R04 about_actor NOT_EVIDENCED -> ENGINEERING, KNOWN); the unmapped counter is never reported; v1 fields are not normalized; the merged record takes R06's lineage/v1 values only (R07's v1 event differs). The merge deletes the only ACT_WITHDRAWN.
fidelity.r3: FAITHFUL. The split at 'rest = open' is correct; the rows wrapper pops v1_t in both datasets and v1_s in NORM only; the r1 tail is executed in ns. All non-target NORM verdicts equal r2's minus the dropped fields.

fixes_justified: Largely yes on the merits, but post hoc. F2 is strongly justified: NORM v1_s = the deontic polarity, and r2's only POSSIBLE pairs were v1_s. F1 is justified: A' target = v1_t on START events, though not for R04/R05 ('own-slice'). However, the fixes were specified after the sealed expectation (NORM target strict) failed, from a diagnostic that prints the blocking fields per pair. They removed only POSSIBLE-blockers for the expected variable, and left the STRICT-blockers shown on every line (unknown_on>=4). Against a tuning charge: they did not also drop v1_a/v1_r, which would have yielded 19 POSSIBLE. r3 should be labelled exploratory.

remaining_duplicates_or_circular.detail: Same concept as A' actor in ACT. In NORM it equals about_actor for START-lineage events but equals the norm-maker (≈ stated_by) where the lineage points to the authorizing act (R04: ARB). It blocks R04 × {R10,R12,R14,R31,R33}. It is not normalized (AUTHORITY vs DECISION-AUTHORITY).
START implies EXECUTION. It differs within same-operation pairs only through the lineage level mismatch (R04: RULING). It co-blocks the R04 pairs.
Coarse target kind (work/ruling/operational-acceptance/'same:' tokens). For a target contrast it is an attribute of the variable under test. It is constant on START and blocks R05~R06 in ACT.
'guards-met' on R04/R05 looks coded from the outcome; check for circularity with act.state before treating it as a guard.
UNK on every START event. v1_h is known only on R25 and v1_c only on R03, so STRICT is unsatisfiable for every variable in every version.

fillable_from_sources.v1_e/x/h/c: No. They are v1-coded, v1 is frozen, and they are likely inapplicable to execution norms ('n/a' is UNKNOWN). They need an instrument change (drop structurally inapplicable fields), not filling.
fillable_from_sources.about_actor R14, R33: Not as SOURCE_FACT from the span. Only as in-section INFERENCE (R-47 'execution responsibility transfers to engineering'; R-58 sibling span 'Engineering is authorized to begin…'), the same grade already accepted for R10/R13.
fillable_from_sources.about_actor R12, R31; stated_by R31: Not feasible from the quoted material (R-79 directive names no actor; the R-56 note's author is unnamed). Filling R31 stated_by=ARB would eliminate R31~R36.
fillable_from_sources.overall: The A' blockers are partly fillable at INFERENCE grade. The STRICT-blockers (v1_e/x/h/c) are not fillable.

interpretation.act_nonidentifiable: PARTLY. 'Not falsified' is correct; the claim is vacuous because STRICT is unreachable. 'Non-identifiable in this corpus' is overstated: it holds under this coding/instrument. The only same-op negative (R06) was deleted by the merge. The 1ayn rule makes negative operations UNMAPPABLE (R29). A' R-A2/R-A3 plus coder choices (R01, R03, R26, R27, R29) converted most v1 REFUSED outcomes (18 of 36 v1 events, many norm-level) into ACT_OCCURRED of other operations.
interpretation.norm_target_possible: PARTLY. POSSIBLE is correct in the instrument's sense, but at most 12 of 14 are genuine (composite artifacts R14~R32, R14~R34), records recur, and cross-section pairs are confounded with time/authorizing ruling. 'Not strict' is by construction, not a finding. The same-target flips R31~R32 and R33~R34 show that target alone does not index polarity.

establishes: r1-r3 are correctly composed; r2/r3 change only what they declare, apart from the listed undeclared side effects.
Under A' coding and 1ay-n normalization the ACT dataset is 23+/1-, so act-level guard contrasts cannot be tested on it.
NORM START-EXECUTION has 5+/5- and up to 12 genuine same-operation, same-actor/stated_by, opposite-polarity pairs that differ in target; 2 of them lie within a single ruling (R13~R14, R32~R33).
The same target flips polarity across successive rulings with all coded fields equal (R31→R32, R33→R34).
does_not_establish: Any STRICT witness or EMPIRICALLY-SUPPORTED/WEAK verdict, or its absence as evidence: STRICT is unreachable by construction.
That act-level guards are absent or non-identifiable in the corpus (as opposed to this coding and merge).
Independence beyond 1-2 clusters for the target pairs.

Any discrimination between rule-making and broad-governance hypotheses: both predict target-specific authorizations; stated_by has 0 POSSIBLE pairs; the discriminating signal (polarity changed by an intervening act/ruling) is not a variable.
Anything resting on v1 fields beyond V1-CODED weight.
